job.title: Senior Contract Administrator
job.description:
Senior Contracts Administrator | High-Rise Residential
Brisbane Northside
 
The Company
This privately owned Brisbane builder has built a strong reputation for delivering high-quality residential and mixed-use developments across South East Queensland.
 
With close to three decades of experience, the business has established long-standing relationships with developers, consultants and subcontractors, with a significant proportion of its work coming from repeat clients. The company takes a selective approach to its project pipeline, allowing its teams to maintain a strong focus on quality, delivery and client relationships.
 
With an exciting pipeline of large-scale high-rise residential developments, including projects extending beyond $200m, they are now looking to appoint an experienced Senior Contracts Administrator to join their Brisbane team.
 
The Role
Working within a lean, high-performing project team, you will take ownership of the commercial and contractual requirements of a major residential development.
 
This is an opportunity to operate with genuine autonomy and visibility, working closely with the Project Manager, site team, subcontractors and senior leadership.
 
Your responsibilities will include:
  • Procurement and letting of major trade packages
  • Subcontractor negotiations and contract administration
  • Progress claims, variations and cost reporting
  • Forecasting and maintaining project budgets
  • Managing contractual correspondence and documentation
  • Assessing subcontractor claims and variations
  • Identifying and managing commercial risks
  • Working closely with the delivery team to maintain programme and commercial outcomes
  • Building strong relationships with subcontractors, consultants and key stakeholders
  • Supporting junior commercial team members where required
About You
We are looking for an experienced CA who understands the pace, complexity and commercial requirements of delivering major residential construction.
 
Ideally, you will bring:
  • Previous experience as a Senior Contracts Administrator or experienced Contracts Administrator
  • High-rise residential or major apartment experience strongly preferred
  • Experience on projects valued at $50m+
  • Strong subcontractor procurement and negotiation capability
  • Sound understanding of construction contracts, variations and claims
  • Strong commercial awareness and cost management skills
  • Ability to operate effectively within a lean project team
  • Relevant construction, quantity surveying or commercial qualification
Why Join?
This opportunity will suit someone who enjoys the capability and standards associated with a larger contractor but prefers the accessibility, autonomy and culture of a leaner business.
 
You'll have the opportunity to work on some of Brisbane's significant residential developments, with the business currently delivering premium multi-residential projects within major inner-Brisbane growth precincts.
 
If you're an experienced Contracts Administrator looking to take greater ownership of major high-rise projects without getting lost within a large corporate structure, I'd be keen to have a confidential conversation.
 
Apply now or contact Monique at Stellar Recruitment for a confidential discussion.

job.title: Project Engineer
job.description:

Key Responsibilities:

  • Supporting project cost management, forecasting and monthly reporting
  • Assisting with variations, claims and other contractual matters
  • Working with subcontractors, suppliers, consultants and clients to resolve technical and delivery issues
What You'll Bring
  • Proven experience in civil construction in a Site Engineer or Project Engineer capacity
  • Strong practical background across three waters, pipelines, or wider civil infrastructure
  • Good commercial awareness including quantities, costs, progress, and forecasting
  • Ability to read and interpret civil drawings, specifications, and contract requirements
  • A practical, solutions-focused approach with the confidence to make decisions in a fast-moving environment
What's on Offer

  • Diverse range of civil projects across the Bay of Plenty
  • Real opportunity to broaden your experience and take on increased responsibility
  • Secure, long-term pipeline of work

This is a strong career move for a civil engineer who enjoys working on interesting and complex projects. Apply now or reach out for a confidential discussion.

job.title: General Manager- Brand, Partnerships & Growth
job.description:
About TIACS

TIACS is Australia’s home of blue-collar counselling, providing free, professional mental health support to tradies, truckies, farmers, apprentices, blue-collar workers and the people who care about them.

No waitlists. No referrals. No cost.

Our mission is to remove the barriers that stop blue-collar Australians from accessing support. Keeping that service free takes strong partnerships, sustainable funding and commercially disciplined growth.

That’s where this role comes in.

You’ll help shape TIACS’ next phase of growth, working closely with the CEO to expand our reach, revenue and impact across Australia.

TIACS - The Home of Blue Collar Counselling By Industry for Industry

The Opportunity

As General Manager – Brand, Partnerships & Growth, you’ll lead the functions that drive TIACS’ financial sustainability, market presence and long-term growth.

Reporting directly to the CEO, you’ll bring together brand, marketing, communications, partnerships, engagement and revenue into one clear growth engine.

You’ll be responsible for building meaningful relationships across industry, strengthening the TIACS Alliance, growing diversified revenue streams and ensuring the TIACS brand continues to connect authentically with blue-collar Australia.

This is a senior leadership position, but it isn’t one for someone who wants to sit above the work.

You’ll need to be equally comfortable shaping strategy with the CEO, building a boardroom case for investment, meeting industry partners and spending time on-site understanding the people and communities TIACS exists to support.

You’ll lead the strategy and delivery across:
  • Brand, Marketing & Engagement
  • Partnerships & Alliance Development
  • Growth & Revenue
  • Leadership & Performance
About You
  • Senior-level experience leading growth, partnerships, brand or revenue functions
  • A strong track record of delivering measurable revenue, fundraising or growth outcomes
  • Deep capability across marketing, communications, digital and social channels
  • Experience developing and managing strategic partnerships with industry, stakeholders or funders
  • Commercial and financial acumen, including pipeline management, forecasting and revenue oversight
  • Experience leading and developing high-performing teams
  • Strong judgement, credibility and the ability to build relationships that last
  • The confidence to operate in both commercial and purpose-driven environments
How to apply:

Apply via SEEK for a confidential discussion.

job.title: Superintendent - Metallurgy
job.description:
• Lead metallurgy, process control and laboratory performance at a major zinc-lead operation
  • Senior leadership role with Glencore’s McArthur River Mine
  • Attractive FIFO roster, competitive remuneration and long-term career opportunities
Stellar Recruitment is partnering with Glencore to appoint a Superintendent – Metallurgy at McArthur River Mine in the Northern Territory.
Located approximately 970 kilometres south-east of Darwin, McArthur River Mine is one of Australia’s largest zinc-lead operations. The site incorporates an open-cut mine, processing facilities and a logistics network transporting concentrate to the Bing Bong Loading Facility for export to customers around the world.

This is an opportunity to take a senior leadership role within a technically complex processing operation and influence plant performance, recovery, product quality and continuous improvement.

The role:

Reporting to the Manager – Metallurgy and Port Operations, the Superintendent – Metallurgy will lead the site’s metallurgical, process-control and laboratory functions.

You will be accountable for ensuring metallurgical systems operate safely and effectively while delivering planned production volumes and product-quality outcomes. The position will provide technical leadership to the metallurgy and laboratory teams and work closely with processing, maintenance, technical and HSE stakeholders.

Key responsibilities will include:
  • Monitor and optimise plant metallurgical performance and process-control systems.
  • Identify performance constraints and coordinate practical remedial actions.
  • Lead the implementation of new process systems, equipment and plant upgrades.
  • Drive improvements in recovery, throughput, stability and concentrate quality.
  • Ensure the metallurgical laboratory operates safely, efficiently and in accordance with required standards.
  • Provide technical direction, coaching and development to metallurgical and laboratory personnel.
  • Lead, mentor and manage a multidisciplinary metallurgy and laboratory team.
  • Contribute to annual business plans, operating budgets, capital budgets and performance reporting.
  • Manage the availability, consumption and cost-effective use of major plant consumables.
  • Support plant trials, technical investigations and improvement projects.
  • Work collaboratively with production, maintenance and HSE teams to deliver safe and sustainable operational outcomes.
About You:

To succeed in this position, you will bring:
  • Tertiary qualifications in Metallurgical, Chemical or Process Engineering, or a closely related discipline.
  • Substantial practical experience within mineral-processing or metallurgical plant operations.
  • Strong knowledge of metallurgical processes, plant optimisation and process-control systems.
  • Experience in complex base-metal concentrators or flotation operations will be highly regarded.
  • Demonstrated leadership experience managing metallurgists, laboratory personnel or processing technical teams.
  • A sound understanding of metallurgical laboratory practices, sampling, analysis and quality control.
  • Experience delivering process-improvement initiatives, plant trials, equipment upgrades or operational projects.
  • Exposure to operating budgets, capital planning, cost control and technical performance reporting.
  • Strong analytical, troubleshooting and decision-making capability.
  • The ability to translate technical findings into clear operational actions.
  • Strong communication and stakeholder-management skills across operational and technical functions.
Benefits:
  • Permanent senior leadership opportunity with Glencore.
  • Attractive FIFO 9 days on 5 days off roster from any capital city
  • Competitive remuneration package and applicable site benefits.
  • Support from an experienced site leadership and technical-services team.
  • Long-term professional development opportunities across Glencore’s Australian and international operations.
  • Work within a large-scale operation offering complex technical challenges and significant scope for improvement.
To Apply:

This recruitment process is being managed by Lucas Eyers at Stellar Recruitment. Please apply via SEEK or LinkedIn or contact Lucas directly to discuss in confidence.

+61 4 5248 3407 or email lucas@stellarrecruitment.com.au

job.title: National Engagement Lead
job.description:
About TIACS

We are all about showing up where it matters — on worksites, in communities, and alongside the people and industries we’re in it with.

We are building one of the most innovative social purpose counselling services in the country and are looking for an experienced National Engagement Lead to join the team.

TIACS is Australia’s home of blue-collar counselling, providing free, confidential and accessible professional support to tradies, truckies, farmers, apprentices, blue-collar workers and the people who care about them.

No waitlists. No referrals. No cost.

This role is about making sure the people who need that support know TIACS exists, trust the service, and know how to access it.

TIACS - The Home of Blue Collar Counselling By Industry for Industry

The role

This is not a desk-based role.

Based in Brisbane, you’ll work nationally across worksites, industry events and community initiatives, building trusted relationships with workers, employers, industry groups and decision-makers.

You’ll lead TIACS’ engagement activity across priority industries and regions, while connecting on-the-ground insights with the broader partnerships strategy to identify opportunities and create longer-term impact.

The role includes regular interstate and regional travel, early starts, evening events and occasional weekend work.

If you enjoy being out with people and building relationships face-to-face, this could be a great fit.

What you’ll be doing
  • Building trusted relationships with workers, employers, supervisors and industry leaders
  • Representing TIACS across worksites, industry events and community activities
  • Delivering practical, relatable engagement that makes mental health support easier to understand and access
  • Building repeat engagement across priority industries and regions
  • Identifying partnership, alliance and fundraising opportunities from conversations in the field
  • Working closely with the Head of Partnerships & Impact to progress opportunities
  • Coordinating national engagement activity, bookings and travel
  • Capturing engagement activity, contacts and insights in HubSpot
  • Sharing on-the-ground themes, barriers and opportunities with the wider TIACS team
  • Supporting and guiding the Industry & Community Engagement Officer where required
Who we’re looking for

You do not need to be a counsellor. This is a non-clinical role.

We’re looking for someone grounded, credible and genuinely good with people.
You might come from a community engagement, partnerships, fundraising or field-based background.

More importantly, you’ll be someone who can walk onto a worksite and connect naturally with the crew, then sit down with senior leaders and hold your own.

You’ll need to be able to:
  • Build trust without relying on a polished sales pitch
  • Communicate naturally with different audiences
  • Handle sensitive conversations with good judgement and clear boundaries
  • Work independently and stay organised across a national travel schedule
  • Follow through on conversations and relationships h
  • Represent TIACS in a way that is authentic, approachable and down to earth
How to apply:

Apply via SEEK for a confidential discussion.

job.title: Parts Correspondent
job.description:
The role:
If you're organised, customer-focused, and passionate about parts, this is a great opportunity to join TDX as a Parts Correspondent. You'll play an important role in managing customer enquiries, processing orders, providing product information, and ensuring parts solutions are delivered efficiently and accurately.

Reporting to the Parts Manager, you will be responsible for interpreting customer enquiries, processing orders accurately, coordinating parts availability, and supporting internal teams to ensure customers receive the highest level of service.

 Responsibilities include:
  • Provide face-to-face, over the phone and email support and advice to our customers to ensure they receive the right part, at the right price, at the right time and place.
  • Interpret & process incoming purchase orders for efficient dispatch
  • Coordinate the dispatch of customer orders within an acceptable time frame, ensuring all documentation requirements are met
  • Quote enquiries, monitor sales orders daily
  • Be committed to providing a quality service to internal and external customers and suppliers
Who are we?
TDX is a true New Zealand success story and 100% New Zealand owned and operated. From humble beginnings when we were set up over 40 years ago by a couple of mates, today TDX is recognised as the market leader for sales and service of construction equipment. We service our highly valued customers in the civil, forestry, construction, mining and marine sectors across all of New Zealand.

TDX is the distributor of leading global brands including Volvo CE, Yanmar CE, Shell Lubricants, Fuchs Kohler Generators, Perkins Engines and Allison Transmissions. We are committed to combining world-class experience with local know-how.

What’s in it for you?
  • Supportive and friendly team environment
  • Ongoing training and development opportunities
  • Weekly pay
  • company bonus
  • On-site parking
  • Discounts on retail products
  • Life insurance
  • Discounted medical insurance
  • Opportunities to grow your career with a market-leading New Zealand-owned business
At TDX, we are passionate about supporting our people and creating a workplace where everyone can succeed. You’ll be part of a team that works together, values each other’s contribution, and is committed to delivering the best possible customer experience every time.

You will ideally have:
  • Previous experience in a parts department or similar customer-focused role
  • Strong attention to detail and excellent organisational skills
  • The ability to manage multiple tasks and meet deadlines
  • Confidence using computer systems, including Microsoft Office
  • A positive and enthusiastic attitude with a willingness to learn
  • The ability to work both independently and as part of a team

If you’re looking for an opportunity to grow your career with a leading New Zealand-owned business and bring your passion for parts and customer service, we’d love to hear from you.

Apply now and become part of the TDX team.

job.title: Maintenance Officer (Workshop Parts)
job.description:
Maintenance Officer (Workshop Parts)
 
Glencore Mount Isa Mines | Mount Isa, QLD | 7 Days On / 7 Days Off (Days Only)
 
Our client, Glencore Mount Isa Mines, is seeking an experienced Maintenance Officer to join their Mobile Maintenance team, supporting the ISF & Rebuild Workshop. This is an excellent opportunity to become part of one of Australia's leading mining operations, playing a vital role in ensuring maintenance activities are supported through the efficient coordination and management of parts and materials.

Working closely with planners, supervisors, leading hands and tradespeople, you'll help keep maintenance schedules on track by ensuring the right parts are available at the right time, while maintaining strong communication across the maintenance and supply teams.
 
About the Role:

You will be responsible for coordinating workshop parts and consumables, supporting maintenance planning activities, and ensuring workshop operations run efficiently.
 
What's on Offer:
  • Join Glencore Mount Isa Mines, one of Australia's premier mining operations.
  • Lifestyle roster of 7 days on / 7 days off (day shift only).
  • Work within a highly experienced Mobile Maintenance team supporting a large surface mining fleet.
  • Ongoing career development and training opportunities.
  • Competitive remuneration and the opportunity to build your career with a respected global mining company.
Your responsibilities:
  • Coordinating the dispatch and receipt of maintenance parts to support workshop rebuild and maintenance activities.
  • Working closely with maintenance planners, supervisors and warehouse personnel to ensure parts are available for scheduled work.
  • Monitoring parts availability and proactively communicating any supply risks or delays.
  • Ordering parts, tracking deliveries and following up outstanding purchase requests.
  • Receiving, inspecting and organizing incoming parts within designated staging areas.
  • Coordinating the collection and delivery of parts and components across the operation.
  • Maintaining workshop consumable stock levels.
  • Managing excess inventory registers and identifying opportunities to reduce surplus stock.
  • Processing catalogue additions and maintaining accurate parts information within SAP.
  • Supporting continuous improvement initiatives that enhance workshop efficiency and reduce waste.
  • Completing general administrative tasks and maintaining accurate maintenance records.
  • Promoting a safe, collaborative and customer-focused working environment in line with Glencore's values.
About You:
  • Previous experience in a maintenance support, workshop administration, stores or parts coordination role within mining or heavy industry.
  • Exposure to mobile mining equipment, heavy earthmoving equipment or heavy vehicle maintenance.
  • Willing to relocate to Mount Isa 
  • Strong organizational skills with the ability to effectively manage competing priorities.
  • Excellent communication and stakeholder engagement skills.
  • The ability to work both independently and within a collaborative maintenance team.
  • Experience using SAP or a similar Computerised Maintenance Management System (CMMS) is highly regarded.
  • Intermediate to advanced Microsoft Office skills.
  • A current manual driver's licence.
  • A current forklift licence, or the willingness to obtain one.

job.title: Senior Associate Commercial
job.description:
About the Role
This is a senior role is suited to a lawyer who enjoys the breadth of private practice and values being more than just a technical specialist.

You'll work closely with business owners, property investors, lenders, private clients, and developers, managing matters from initial instructions through to completion. The practice includes mortgagee sale work as a core component, alongside a mix of property, commercial, trust, private client, and general advisory matters.

The role offers the freedom to manage your own files, build lasting client relationships, and play an active part in the future direction of the practice.

Key Work
  • Advising lenders and stakeholders on mortgagee sales
  • Property acquisitions, disposals, leasing, and development matters
  • Commercial contracts and business transactions
  • Trusts, asset planning, and private client work
  • General legal advisory services for long-standing clients
  • Mentoring junior lawyers where appropriate
  • Contributing to client development and practice growth
What You'll Gain
  • A genuinely broad practice rather than a narrow specialist role
  • Significant client contact and ownership of relationships
  • The ability to make decisions without layers of management
  • Stable, established work with a loyal client base
  • Flexibility and trust in how you manage your workload
  • A clear path toward a leadership position for the right person
  • Competitive remuneration reflecting seniority and contribution
About You
  • 5+ years PQE gained within New Zealand private practice
  • Experience handling mortgagee sale matters
  • Strong grounding across property and commercial law
  • Confidence managing files independently
  • Excellent client relationship and communication skills
  • A practical, commercially minded approach
  • The ability to work across a varied practice rather than a highly specialised caseload
Culture
A collegial & down-to-earth team where senior lawyers are trusted to manage their practice, contribute ideas & build lasting client relationships. The environment suits someone who values autonomy, accessibility & working closely with clients rather than operating within a heavily layered structure.

About the Firm
This established Auckland practice offers the breadth of work often associated with a larger platform while maintaining the accessibility & flexibility of a boutique environment. Lawyers enjoy direct client engagement, meaningful responsibility & the opportunity to become an integral part of the firm's long-term future.

job.title: Commercial Litigation Lawyer
job.description:
One of New Zealand's most respected litigation teams is looking for a lawyer around the three-year mark to take on a caseload focused on insolvency and restructuring work in Auckland. The work is genuinely complex, the clients are high-calibre, and this team has a serious reputation in the market. You will need a litigation background to hit the ground running here, and some existing R&I exposure will put you ahead of the field.

The Role
You will be working across the full spectrum of restructuring and insolvency, from formal insolvencies and workouts through to distressed M&A, enforcement, and cross-border matters. There is also a steady stream of commercial disputes work in the mix, so you won't be limited to just insolvency matters. Clients include banks, credit funds, insolvency practitioners, corporate borrowers, and directors, both domestic and international.

Key Work 
  • Formal insolvency appointments and enforcement
  • Workouts, turnarounds, and distressed refinancings
  • Cross-border restructuring matters
  • Distressed M&A transactions
  • Director liability and third-party claims
  • Commercial disputes alongside the core R&I caseload
Day to Day Responsibilities   
  • Advising a sophisticated client base on complex insolvency and restructuring matters
  • Court engagement and preparation across a range of proceedings
  • Drafting pleadings, opinions, and transactional documents
  • Working across practice groups on multi-disciplinary matters
  • Running your own files with partner support when you need it
About You 
  • Around three years of New Zealand litigation experience, with some R&I exposure preferred
  • Comfortable in court and confident drafting pleadings and litigation documents
  • Strong academics; you will be asked for your transcript
  • Someone who writes well, thinks clearly, and does not need to be told twice
  • Comfortable working independently, but knows when to ask questions
What's on Offer   
  • Wellbeing allowance to spend however it is most useful to you
  • Flexible working and a home office allowance
  • Generous parental leave with structured support on the way in and out
  • Public transport benefit, late-night travel and meals covered when needed
  • Some flexibility around leave, including the option to purchase additional days
About the Firm 
A full-service national firm with a well-established litigation team and a restructuring and insolvency practice that carries genuine weight in the market. The team handles high-complexity domestic and cross-border work at volume, and the broader litigation group keeps things varied. This is a firm that takes development seriously and tends to attract lawyers who want to be stretched.

How to Apply
Please send your CV and academic transcripts to jenny.g@stellarrecruitment.co.nz or call 021 0230 3960 for a confidential discussion.

Please include your academic transcript with your CV, as this forms part of the initial review.

We are seeking an experienced Production Engineer to join our client based in Christchurch. You will play a key role in optimising production systems, supporting workshop staff, driving continuous improvement initiatives, and ensuring compliance with quality and safety standards.

  • Supporting the implementation of new equipment and technology
  • Assisting with production planning and scheduling activities

  • Possess a strong understanding of production planning, workflow optimisation, and manufacturing processes
  • Experience driving continuous improvement and efficiency initiatives
  • Ability to read and interpret engineering drawings and technical documentation
  • Knowledge of quality assurance systems and manufacturing standards
  • Understanding of Health & Safety legislation and safe work practices
  • Strong problem-solving and root cause analysis skills
  • Excellent communication and interpersonal abilities

job.title: Site Supervisor - Energy Sector
job.description:
Construction Site Supervisor - Industrial Projects
North Island - Full-Time - Industrial Construction
Are you an experienced Construction Site Supervisor with a proven track record delivering projects in petrochemical, oil & gas, energy, process plant, or heavy industrial environments?
  
We're seeking an experienced, hands-on leader to take ownership of site operations, lead construction crews and subcontractors and deliver complex industrial projects safely, efficiently and to a high standard. This senior site leadership role offers genuine autonomy, long-term career prospects and the opportunity to work alongside experienced engineering, project management, quality and HSE teams.
  
About the Role
Reporting into the project team, you'll be responsible for the day-to-day supervision and coordination of site activities across a range of industrial construction projects.
  
Key responsibilities include:
  • Lead and supervise mechanical, piping, structural steel and civil construction activities.
  • Manage site crews, subcontractors and specialist contractors.
  • Coordinate labour, plant, materials and daily work fronts.
  • Champion a strong health, safety and environmental culture.
  • Oversee permit-to-work systems, isolations and high-risk activities.
  • Conduct pre-start meetings, toolbox talks and site briefings.
  • Monitor project progress, productivity and programme performance.
  • Coordinate quality, testing, commissioning and compliance requirements.
  • Manage subcontractor performance, site documentation, reporting and client relationships.
  
About You
To be successful in this role, you'll have:
  • Significant construction supervision experience within industrial, petrochemical, oil & gas, energy or process plant environments.
  • Strong knowledge of mechanical construction and site operations.
  • Experience overseeing piping, structural steel, pressure equipment and mechanical installations.
  • Sound understanding of permit-to-work systems, isolations and high-risk work activities.
  • Strong leadership, communication and people management skills.
  • Proven ability to coordinate multiple work fronts and manage competing priorities.
  • Experience working with clients, engineers, subcontractors and project teams.
  • Good understanding of construction drawings, specifications, QA/QC processes and inspections.
  • Knowledge of NZ HSE requirements and industry standards, with trade qualifications and relevant site certifications highly regarded.
  
What's on Offer?
  • Senior site leadership role with genuine authority and responsibility.
  • Exposure to complex industrial, petrochemical, energy and process plant projects.
  • Strong pipeline of ongoing project and maintenance work.
  • Well-supported environment backed by experienced engineering, QA/QC, project management and HSE teams.

job.title: Business Support Administrator | Manufacturing
job.description:
Business Support Administrator | Manufacturing
Lower Hutt | Permanent | Full-Time | Monday to Friday
  
If you’re organised, practical and enjoy working in a busy environment where there’s always something happening, this could be a great fit.
  
Our client is an established Lower Hutt-based business operating in a hands-on engineering environment. Their administration team plays a key role in keeping the wider business running smoothly, and they’re looking for someone reliable who can come in, pick things up quickly and become a trusted part of the team.
  
This is a varied business support role with a strong accounts focus, alongside purchasing, timesheet administration and general office support. It would suit someone who enjoys being across different areas of a business and is comfortable working at pace.
  
What you’ll be doing
  • Processing supplier invoices and day-to-day accounts administration
  • Matching invoices, purchase orders and delivery dockets
  • Entering accruals and maintaining accurate financial records
  • Supporting purchasing across a range of business requirements
  • Liaising with suppliers and internal teams
  • Checking and collating weekly timesheets for payroll processing
  • Working within an ERP system and keeping information accurate
  • Resolving discrepancies and following up outstanding information
  • Providing general administration support across the wider business
What we’re looking for
  
You’ll ideally have previous experience in accounts administration, purchasing or wider business support, particularly within manufacturing, engineering, construction, logistics or another operational environment.
  
You’ll need to be confident working with invoices and financial information, comfortable handling a steady workload and able to maintain accuracy when things get busy.
  
Some purchasing experience would be valuable, along with the ability to understand what is being ordered, why it is needed and how it fits into the wider operation.
  
Experience using an ERP system is also important. We’re open on the specific platform, as long as you’re comfortable learning systems, following processes and working through something that may not always be particularly user-friendly.
  
Payroll experience is useful but doesn’t need to be extensive. The payroll side of the role is primarily focused on checking and collating timesheets before they are sent through to an external provider.
  
You’ll suit this role if you’re someone who:
  • Is reliable and takes pride in getting the job done
  • Enjoys being busy and naturally looks for what needs doing next
  • Has strong attention to detail
  • Is confident communicating with different personalities
  • Can manage competing priorities without getting flustered
  • Is practical, resilient and comfortable in a hands-on environment
  • Is happy to jump in and support the wider team when needed
What’s on offer
  • Permanent, full-time opportunity

  • Lower Hutt location
  • Varied role across accounts, purchasing, payroll support and administration
  • Established operational environment
  • Plenty of responsibility and variety day to day
  • Opportunity to become a valued part of a close-working team
If you’re an experienced administrator who enjoys a busy environment, likes having plenty to do and is comfortable working alongside operational teams, we’d love to hear from you.

job.title: Health & Safety Advisor
job.description:
Our client is delivering a significant solar farm development in the Taupō region and is seeking a Health & Safety Advisor to join the site team on a permanent basis.

This is a junior to intermediate-level position focused on providing practical, hands-on health and safety support throughout the construction phase. You will work closely with an experienced Senior Health & Safety professional, project leadership and site teams to maintain safe working practices and support a positive safety culture.

The role is based in Taupō. Candidates may relocate to the region or work an 11/3 roster on a FIFO or DIDO basis.

Key Responsibilities:
  • Provide practical, site-based health and safety advice and support
  • Conduct site inspections, observations and safety conversations
  • Assist with hazard identification, risk assessments and control measures
  • Support site inductions, toolbox talks and ongoing safety training
  • Help maintain health and safety documentation, registers and reporting
  • Participate in incident investigations and corrective action processes
  • Engage with employees, subcontractors and project leaders at all levels
  • Work alongside the Senior Health & Safety professional to promote a strong safety culture
  • Support compliance with project procedures and relevant health and safety requirements
What you will bring:

You will have a solid foundation in health and safety and some experience working in a site-based construction or industrial environment. You will be comfortable engaging directly with the workforce and providing practical guidance in an active project setting.

To be successful, you will ideally bring:
  • Junior to intermediate-level health and safety experience
  • Proven site-based experience in construction or a similar industrial environment
  • A practical and visible approach to health and safety
  • The confidence to influence safe behaviours and address issues constructively
  • Strong communication and relationship-building skills
  • The ability to engage effectively with workers, subcontractors and project leadership
  • Sound organisational, documentation and reporting skills
  • A construction background, although other substantial site-based experience will be considered
Preferred Qualifications
  • National Certificate or Diploma in Health and Safety, or an equivalent recognised qualification
  • Current First Aid certificate
  • Membership with NZISM or another relevant professional body
What’s on Offer
  • A permanent position on a significant renewable energy construction project
  • Direct exposure to a large-scale, active project environment
  • Support and professional development from an experienced Senior Health & Safety professional
  • The opportunity to build your capability within the growing renewable energy sector
  • Taupō-based work with relocation, FIFO or DIDO options
  • An 11/3 roster for candidates working away from home

job.title: Senior Exploration Geologist
job.description:
Discover What's Next.
 
Are you a discovery-focused exploration geologist with a passion for target generation and building exploration pipelines that deliver results?
 
We are seeking an experienced Senior Exploration Geologist to join a well-funded exploration team and drive target generation across a highly prospective Western Australian gold province. This is a genuine generative exploration role where you'll have the backing, autonomy and resources to identify, advance and test high-quality opportunities.
 
If you've built drill-ready targets within the Yilgarn, understand regolith systems, and enjoy the challenge of making discoveries, we'd love to hear from you.
 
About the Role
 
Reporting to the Exploration Manager, you will play a key role in generating and advancing exploration targets from concept through to drill testing.
 
Key Responsibilities
  • Generate and mature high-quality drill-ready targets
  • Build and prioritise a pipeline of exploration opportunities
  • Integrate geological, geochemical, geophysical and regolith datasets
  • Conduct geological and structural interpretations
  • Design and oversee drilling programs
  • Interpret drilling results and recommend follow-up programs
  • Produce technical reports and exploration models
  • Maintain QA/QC standards and data integrity
  • Lead field activities, contractors and junior geologists
  • Ensure compliance with safety, environmental and heritage requirements
About You
  • Degree qualified in Geology
  • Minimum 5+ years' experience in a Senior Exploration Geologist capacity
  • Strong experience working within the Yilgarn Craton
  • Proven target generation and discovery-focused exploration experience
  • Strong understanding of regolith geology and regolith-based exploration techniques
  • Demonstrated success generating drill-ready targets
  • Excellent structural geology and geological interpretation skills
  • Experience with Leapfrog, Micromine, QGIS and/or MapInfo
  • Knowledge of WA mining regulations and JORC requirements
  • Current WA Manual Driver's Licence
What's on Offer
  • Discovery-focused role with genuine exploration upside
  • Strong technical and financial support
  • Large prospective land package with significant growth potential
  • Opportunity to influence exploration strategy and target generation
  • Collaborative and experienced exploration team
  • Competitive salary and long-term career opportunities
 
Apply Now
 
If you're a discovery-driven geologist with a proven track record in target generation, Yilgarn gold systems and regolith exploration, this is an opportunity to make a genuine impact and help uncover the next major gold discovery.

job.title: Environmental Officer - Greenfield Mining Project
job.description:
About the opportunity

Stellar Recruitment is partnering with an Australian mining company to recruit an Environmental Officer for a greenfield critical minerals project near Mudgee.

This is an opportunity to join during the development phase and help establish the environmental systems, plans and processes that will support the project as it progresses. You’ll work within an experienced environmental team, with exposure to senior management and scope to develop your expertise across a broad range of environmental disciplines.

The project is progressing through the approvals process, with groundworks targeted for 2028, subject to approvals. The proposed mining operation involves a single open pit and day-shift mining, with substantial company-owned landholdings in the surrounding area.

About the role

Reporting to the Environmental Superintendent, you’ll combine environmental management system development with monitoring, reporting and biodiversity-related activities. Rather than simply maintaining established systems, you’ll have the opportunity to help build them.

A key focus will be developing practical management plans, procedures, forms, registers and processes, alongside supporting biodiversity management across the company’s properties.

Your responsibilities will include:
  • Contributing to the development and implementation of the environmental management system.
  • Supporting biodiversity assessments, monitoring programs and management of biodiversity properties.
  • Coordinating environmental inspections and monitoring across water, air quality, noise, heritage and biodiversity.
  • Interpreting environmental data, preparing reports and supporting regulatory compliance.
  • Working with internal teams, consultants and contractors to translate environmental obligations into practical actions.
About you

You’ll be an environmental professional who enjoys variety, works well independently and is comfortable building relationships across different teams. Experience in mining is welcome, but backgrounds in resources, construction, infrastructure or a regulatory environment will also be considered.

Ideally, you’ll bring a relevant qualification in Environmental Science, Environmental Management or a related discipline, together with experience developing environmental management systems and interpreting environmental requirements. Strong written communication, organisation and stakeholder engagement skills will be important.

Experience managing biodiversity properties, coordinating biodiversity assessments or monitoring programs, and working with the NSW Biodiversity Conservation Act 2016 will be particularly well regarded.

What’s on offer

An attractive remuneration package aligned with your experience, a supportive environmental team and the opportunity to broaden your expertise as the project develops.

You’ll work a 9-day fortnight, with accommodation available for the first six months to help you settle into the area. Set among rolling green hills and established rural communities, this opportunity would suit someone looking to build a career and a life in the Mudgee region.

Long-term residence in the area is required, although relocation does not need to happen immediately. There is flexibility to make the move over the first six to twelve months, allowing time to plan the transition.

How to apply

To express your interest, submit your resume through SEEK. For a confidential discussion about the role and relocation arrangements, contact the team at Stellar Recruitment.

job.title: Senior Mining Engineer - Short Term Planning
job.description:
• FIFO 8/6 Brisbane or Townsville OR Residential Mt Isa
  • Senior Mining Engineer - George Fisher Mine - large scale U/G lead / zinc
  • Attractive salary and benefits package
The operation:
  
George Fisher Mine (GFM) is a large-scale underground zinc-lead-silver operation based in Mt Isa, QLD. GFM has complex mining sequence, multiple operating fronts, and significant interactions among development, stoping, ventilation, backfill, infrastructure, services, and production readiness.
  
George Fisher has a long mine life and is a key strategic asset for Glencore globally.
  
The role:
  
The Senior Mining Engineer – Short Term Planning is responsible for leading and overseeing the preparation and delivery of short-term mine designs and plans to support the safe and efficient execution of development, production, services, and infrastructure activities
  
Your ability to translate medium- and long-term mine plans into practical short-term execution strategies aligned with operational capabilities and production targets will the crucial. We also need someone who can provide technical leadership and guidance to the mining engineering team and also optimise mine design / planning and drill and blast practices.
  
Experience required:
  • Tertiary qualifications in Mining Engineering or related subject
  • Minimum 6–8 years mining engineering experience, preferably within underground hard rock operations
  • Demonstrated experience in short-term mine planning, drill and blast design, and operational mine design.
  • Experience leading or mentoring engineering teams, graduates, or cadets.
  • Practical operational exposure with a strong understanding of underground mining methods and production processes.
  • Strong experience with mine design software such as Surpac, Vulcan, Datamine, or Deswik.
  • Advanced knowledge of drill and blast design, stope design, and operational mine planning.
Benefits on offer:
  • Permanent position working directly for Glencore.
  • Competitive salary package including 13% super, generous incentive scheme.
  • Access to training and professional development
  • Opportunity to work for a large mining company with opportunities to advance your career domestically and internationally.
  • Visa sponsorship available for suitability qualified candidates
  • FIFO to Mt Isa from Brisbane or Townsville or Mt Isa residential
Next Steps:
  
Glencore has partnered with Stellar Recruitment to manage the recruitment and search for this position. Please contact Lucas Eyers to discuss further or apply direct via email / SEEK / LinkedIn

job.title: Human Resources Manager
job.description:
Harmony is the largest gold producer by volume in South Africa and is a significant operator of gold tailings retreatment facilities. CSA Mine has recently joined Harmony Australasia, marking the beginning of an exciting new chapter. The acquisition underpins Harmony’s strategy to expand its Australasian footprint and establish a strong, diversified copper portfolio, complemented by the Eva Copper Mine Project in Queensland, currently under construction, and set to become the state’s largest open‑pit copper mine upon commissioning. In Papua New Guinea, Harmony owns and operates the Hidden Valley mine and owns 50% of the Tier 1 Wafi-Golpu copper-gold project. These assets are supported by the Harmony Australasia regional corporate office located in Milton, Brisbane.
  
About The Role:

The Human Resources Manager – CSA Mine is responsible for delivering end‑to‑end HR leadership at the mine site. Working closely with and reporting to the site General Manager, this role supports safe and productive operations through effective workforce planning, industrial and employee relations, compliance with Australian employment legislation, and the development of a high‑performing workforce.
  
CSA Mine has a workforce of over 500 + contractors and there is also a site-based HR support team. The workforce consists of a mix of residential, DIDO and FIFO. 
  
Roster:
  
This role will be based onsite in Cobar, NSW working an 8/6-day FIFO roster from Brisbane or Sydney with local candidates highly regarded. Local candidates will be offered this opportunity on a 5/2 Monday to Friday roster.
  
Key Responsibilities:
  • Act as a trusted HR advisor to the Site General Manager and leadership team.
  • Deliver site‑based HR strategies aligned with operational and production objectives.
  • Translate corporate HR policies into practical site‑specific solutions.
  • Lead the onsite HR function, ensuring consistent and high‑quality service delivery.
  • Manage employee relations matters including performance management, grievances, investigations, and disciplinary processes.
  • Interpret and apply site enterprise agreements, awards, and contracts.
  • Support or lead enterprise agreement negotiations as required.
  • Liaise effectively with unions, employee representatives, and external advisors.
  • Lead the team that oversees end‑to‑end recruitment for site roles.
  • Manage onboarding, mobilisation, site inductions, and compliance requirements.
  • Partner with site leaders on workforce planning, succession, and talent retention.
  • Support roster structures, FIFO/DIDO and residential arrangements, and fatigue management considerations.
  • Support psychosocial risk management and employee wellbeing initiatives.
  • Partner with HSE teams to ensure people‑related safety obligations are met.
  • Implement performance management and development frameworks.
  • Identify capability gaps and support training and development initiatives.
  • Drive engagement and retention strategies.
  • Support leadership development and workforce capability uplift.
  • Ensure compliance with the Fair Work Act, WHS legislation, and company policies.
  • Maintain accurate HR records, reporting, and dashboards.
  • Support audits, inspections, and regulatory requirements.
  • Contribute to continuous improvement of HR systems and processes.
  • Promote a respectful, inclusive, and values‑driven site culture.
  • Support diversity and inclusion initiatives, including Indigenous engagement where applicable.
  • Act as a role model for company values and leadership behaviours.
About You:

To succeed in this role, you should be self-motivated and able to work efficiently and collaboratively in a team environment with the following skills, experience and personal attributes:
  • Tertiary qualification in Human Resources, Industrial Relations, Business, or related discipline.
  • Significant HR leadership experience within mining, resources, or heavy industry environments.
  • Strong knowledge of Australian employment law, industrial relations, and WHS requirements.
  • Proven experience supporting site workforces in remote operations.
  • Demonstrated ability to influence senior site leaders and manage complex employee relations.
  • Experience in unionised environments and enterprise bargaining.
  • Exposure to large‑scale workforce mobilisation.
  • Prior site‑based HR management experience.
  • Practical, resilient, and outcomes‑focused.
  • Strong communicator with credibility across operational teams.
  • High integrity, discretion, and sound judgement.
  • Collaborative, hands‑on leadership style.
What are the benefits of working for Harmony?
  • The opportunity to work for an international mining company with a diverse workforce.
  • Participation in the company bonus scheme.
  • Health and wellbeing initiatives, including access to gym and pool facilities to our employees and their dependants.
  • Join a business that is growing in Australia and exposed to the high growth commodities of copper and gold.
To learn more about Harmony and CSA Mine, please visit: https://www.harmony.co.za/operations/australia/csa-copper-mine/

• 2/2 or 8/6 Roster FIFO
  • Attractive Remuneration + STIP
  • Various points of hire
Great maintenance starts with great planning.
Stellar Recruitment is proud to partner with Glencore's McArthur River Mine in the search for an experienced Mobile Maintenance Planner.

This is an opportunity for a strong maintenance professional (SAP experience desired yet not essential) to join a large-scale mining operation where quality planning directly impacts equipment availability, productivity and performance.

Working closely with maintenance supervisors, trades and operational stakeholders, you'll help ensure labour, parts, tooling and work scopes come together before the job hits the workshop.

What's on offer
  • Choice of 2/2 or 8/6 roster
  • FIFO travel arrangements, or a $10,500 Darwin allowance
  • Attractive remuneration package plus STIP

job.description:
With the Wellington Civil Construction sector set for a massive 2026, we're on the hunt for experienced Machine Operators to join the ever-growing list of projects across the region. What we're looking for:

  • Temporary to permanent opportunities

job.title: Product Specialist - SCADA Solutions
job.description:
Product Specialist – SCADA Solutions

Join a Trusted Leader in Utilities Technology
We are seeking an experienced Product Specialist to provide technical leadership across our RTU, SCADA and Data Acquisition portfolio and become a trusted advisor to our customers.

About the Role
This is a unique opportunity for a technically capable professional who enjoys combining engineering expertise with customer engagement.
Working closely with utility customers, consultants, engineers and internal stakeholders, you will support the full customer lifecycle—from solution design and technical consultation through to implementation, commissioning and ongoing support.

As the technical face, you'll build trusted relationships, influence key decision-makers and ensure customers receive solutions that meet both technical requirements and operational expectations.

Key Responsibilities
  • Act as the subject matter expert for RTU, SCADA and Data Acquisition solutions.
  • Support customers with technical advice and solution recommendations.
  • Deliver technical presentations, demonstrations and workshops.
  • Assist with solution design, specification and implementation activities.
  • Support commissioning and configuration of RTU, gateway and SCADA systems.
  • Provide guidance on communications, networking and cybersecurity requirements.
  • Work alongside commercial teams to support customer opportunities.
  • Develop long-term relationships built on technical credibility and trust.
  • Stay current with emerging technologies, industry standards and best practice.
About You
You are an experienced engineering or technical professional who enjoys solving complex challenges and working directly with customers.

Ideally you will have:
  • An Electrical Engineering degree or equivalent industry experience.
  • At least 5 years' experience within the power utility, electrical infrastructure or industrial automation sector.
  • Experience working with real-time systems and operational technologies.
  • Strong presentation and communication skills.
  • The ability to work independently while managing multiple priorities.
Technical knowledge in the following areas is highly desirable:
  • SCADA or related architectures
  • RTU and gateway technologies
  • Data acquisition and telemetry systems
  • Monitoring and data logging solutions
  • DNP3, GOOSE and other utility communication protocols
  • IEC61850, ICCP and cybersecurity principles
  • Device configuration and commissioning
  • IP networking and communications infrastructure
What Will Make You Successful?
  • You will be someone who:
  • Builds strong customer relationships and credibility
  • Communicates technical concepts clearly and confidently
  • Demonstrates excellent problem-solving skills
  • Takes ownership and accountability for outcomes
  • Is highly organised and self-managing
  • Maintains a strong focus on customer service and continuous improvement
  • Promotes a positive health and safety culture
Apply Now
If you're passionate about utility automation, SCADA systems and helping customers achieve successful technology outcomes, we'd love to hear from you.

Submit your application today with your CV and a brief cover letter outlining your relevant experience. And/or call nathan.p@stellarrecruitment.co.nz
021 279 4390

job.title: Programme Manager | Power and Distribution
job.description:
Programme Manager | Power and Distribution

Cromwell based (Easy commute from Queenstown, Wānaka or Alexandra)

Lead major infrastructure programmes in the heart of Central Otago

Our client is seeking an experienced Programme Manager to join their Power and Communication Services team based in Cromwell. This is a senior leadership opportunity responsible for overseeing project management, planning, design estimation, scheduling, commercial performance, and operational delivery across a significant portfolio of electrical distribution and infrastructure projects.

About the Role
Reporting to the Regional Manager, you will lead a team of approximately 11 direct reports while coordinating project management, design, estimating and scheduling functions to ensure efficient delivery of annual work programmes. You'll play a key role in resource planning, commercial management, stakeholder engagement, and project execution, while acting as the 2IC for the Regional Manager.
Key responsibilities include:
  • Leading and developing high-performing project, planning and scheduling teams
  • Managing annual and 12-month rolling work programmes
  • Overseeing project delivery, commercial performance and resource utilisation
  • Building strong client and stakeholder relationships
  • Driving health, safety and risk management excellence
  • Supporting budgeting, forecasting and operational planning
  • Leading project reviews, reporting and continuous improvement initiatives
  • Ensuring projects are delivered safely, on time, within budget and to client expectations.  
About You
To be successful, you will bring:
  • 10+ years' experience leading complex infrastructure, construction or engineering projects
  • Strong commercial and contractual expertise
  • Proven leadership experience managing multidisciplinary teams
  • Experience within electrical distribution, utilities, construction or a related industry
  • Excellent stakeholder engagement and relationship management skills
  • Strong planning, scheduling and resource management capability
  • A relevant Engineering, Electrical Trade or Project Management qualification
  • Sound knowledge of risk management and project delivery frameworks.
What's on Offer
  • Senior leadership role with significant influence and responsibility
  • Opportunity to shape and lead major infrastructure programmes
  • Diverse portfolio of projects across Central Otago
  • Collaborative and values-driven culture
  • Long-term career growth within a respected New Zealand organisation
  • If you're a commercially savvy leader with a passion for delivering infrastructure projects and developing high-performing teams, we'd love to hear from you.
Apply now and contact nathan.p@stellarrecruitment.co.nz or 021 279 4390  Stellar Recruitment for a confidential discussion.

job.title: Afternoon Forklift Operator
job.description:
Join a leading Australian steel manufacturer offering stable work, great team culture, and long-term career opportunities.

If you're an experienced forklift operator who enjoys staying active and wants ongoing work with permanent opportunities, this is the role for you.

What's on Offer?
  • Consistent Monday to Friday morning shift roster
  • Early Friday finish at 6pm
  • Ongoing full-time hours with long-term job security
  • Opportunity to secure a permanent position
  • Work for a nationally recognised steel manufacturing business
  • Strong safety culture and supportive team environment
  • Training provided on gantry cranes and site-specific equipment
  • Rate $37.16
Day Shift:
  • Monday to Thursday: 2pm-10:30pm
  • Friday: 12pm - 6pm
The Role Due to ongoing growth, we're seeking experienced Forklift Operators / Production Loaders to join a busy Brisbane manufacturing facility.
Working primarily with steel roofing, walling products and sheet metal materials, you'll play a key role in loading, unloading, moving stock, and supporting production operations in a fast-paced environment.

Key Responsibilities:
  • Operating forklifts to move steel coils, sheet metal, and finished products
  • Loading and unloading trucks with oversized steel products
  • Supporting production lines by feeding and removing materials
  • Completing load restraint and strapping duties
  • Loading steel coils onto manufacturing equipment
  • Operating gantry cranes (training provided)
  • Working closely with dispatch and production teams to meet daily targets
  • Maintaining safe work practices and a clean work environment
What We're Looking For:
  • Current LF Forklift Licence
  • Previous experience operating forklifts in manufacturing, transport, warehouse, yard, or steel environments
  • Experience handling long-length, oversized, or awkward loads
  • Knowledge of load restraint and safe loading practices
  • Strong focus on safety and teamwork
  • Physically fit and comfortable with hands-on duties
  • Reliable, punctual, and committed to morning shift work
  • Gantry crane experience highly regarded but not essential

job.title: Quality Controller
job.description:
About the Role
Reporting to the Production Manager, you will be responsible for ensuring products consistently meet quality standards throughout the manufacturing process. Working as the dedicated Quality Controller on your shift, you will carry out mechanical testing, pressure testing, dimensional testing, inspections and quality documentation to ensure products meet both customer and company requirements.

This is a hands-on role that involves spending time in the production environment working closely with operators and production teams. You will be responsible for recording inspection and test data, supporting production with quality processes, identifying non-conformances and contributing to continuous improvement initiatives across the site.

We are also recruiting for Machine Operators on the rotating shifts too. If you have manufacturing experience and are interested in operating automated production machinery, we would also love to hear from you.

The shift pattern operates on a rotational basis, changing each week. This provides exposure to additional training opportunities and Health & Safety initiatives across all shifts.

The shift patterns are:
  • Day Shift: Monday - Friday 06:00AM - 02:00PM
  • Afternoon Shift: Monday - Friday 02:00PM - 10:00PM
  • Night Shift: Monday Night - Saturday Morning 10:00PM - 06:00AM
Key Requirements & Responsibilities
  • Previous Quality Control experience within a manufacturing environment
  • Experience conducting inspections, testing and quality documentation
  • Strong attention to detail and commitment to quality standards
  • Good literacy and numeracy skills
  • Ability to identify and communicate quality issues
  • Strong understanding of Health & Safety procedures
  • Confident working with production teams and following processes
  • Reliable transport to and from work
  • Positive attitude and willingness to learn
  • Able to pass a pre-employment drug test
  • No serious criminal convictions
About the Company

Our client is a leading manufacturer of plastic pipeline solutions used across New Zealand's civil, plumbing, rural and infrastructure sectors. The business has a strong health & safety culture, values training & development and long-term career growth.

How to Apply Click 'APPLY' or contact Meg Williams if you have any further questions regarding the above.

Email: meg.w@stellarrecruitment.co.nz

job.title: Class 5 Truck Driver | Road Survey Technician
job.description:
About the Client
Our client operates across New Zealand and Australia, delivering innovative transport and road surveying solutions that help maintain and improve the country's road network through advanced data collection technology.

About the Opportunity
We are seeking a Road Survey Technician to join a specialist team responsible for collecting critical road condition data across New Zealand.

This is a highly field-based role, with approximately 20 days per month spent travelling and working on the road network across the country.

Working in a two-person crew, you'll alternate between driving a Class 5 survey vehicle and operating advanced surveying technology from the passenger seat. A significant part of the role involves managing and monitoring data collection systems, ensuring accurate information is captured to support road maintenance and infrastructure planning nationwide.

This is an excellent opportunity for someone who enjoys a mix of technology, travel, and hands-on work, rather than being on the road purely as a truck driver.
 
Benefits
  • $40-$42 per hour 
  • Daily meal allowance of $110
  • Accommodation paid while travelling
  • Travel throughout New Zealand
  • Work with innovative surveying and data collection technology
  • Unique role combining driving, technology, and road infrastructure
About You
  • Minimum 2 years' Class 5 driving experience in New Zealand or Australia
  • Clean driving record
  • Tech-savvy with confidence using software and computer-based systems
  • Strong attention to detail and ability to follow processes
  • Reliable, adaptable, and comfortable travelling for work
  • Enjoy working closely as part of a two-person team

job.title: Civil Supervisor
job.description:
Join a proudly West Australian civil contractor delivering quality subdivision, drainage, utilities and road construction projects across the Perth metro area.
We’re looking for an experienced Civil Supervisor to take ownership of local civil projects either north or south of the river, depending on your home location. This is a permanent opportunity with a respected WA business that values practical leadership, safe delivery and strong relationships on site.

Why this role?
  • Perth metro projects with a stable WA contractor.
  • Subdivision, land development, drainage, utilities, sand import and road construction works.
  • Competitive package of up to $160K + super + company vehicle.
  • Join a business focused on civil construction, where you can thrive!
The opportunity

As Civil Supervisor you’ll supervise daily site activity across Perth metro civil projects, coordinating crews, subcontractors, plant, materials and suppliers while keeping works moving safely, efficiently and to program.

What you’ll be doing
  • Supervise civil crews across subdivisions, drainage, utilities, earthworks and road construction.
  • Coordinate subcontractors, plant, materials and site logistics.
  • Drive safety, quality, productivity and day-to-day program outcomes.
  • Work closely with Project Managers, Engineers, clients and local authorities.
  • Lead from the front and maintain strong site standards and culture.
About you
  • Proven experience as a Civil Supervisor, Foreman or strong Leading Hand ready to step up.
  • Background in Perth metro civil works, ideally subdivisions/land development, roads, drainage and underground services.
  • WA civil construction experience preferred.
  • Experience with contractors such as Georgiou, Wormall Civil, TRACC or similar will be highly regarded.
  • WA manual driver’s licence and White Card required.
  • *Existing work rights for Australia
What’s on offer
  • Up to $160K Base + Super, depending on experience.
  • Company vehicle provided
  • Local Perth metro work with a proudly WA civil contractor, no FIFO!
  • Long-term opportunity with a stable and supportive team.
To be considered, you’ll bring extensive Perth metro Civil Supervision experience across road construction, subdivisions and underground services, ideally gained over 5-10 years with similar civil contractors.

How to apply

job.description:

If you're looking for long-term job security, excellent earning potential and the opportunity to work on a modern mining fleet, we'd love to hear from you.

  • 2/1 or 2/2 rosters available

  • Short Term Incentive Bonus of up to 15% of your base salary, paid twice yearly
  • Additional site, health & wellbeing and commuting allowances

  • Genuine long-term career progression with a major owner-operator

Design Manager
Fortitude Valley, Brisbane | Permanent Full-Time

An exciting opportunity is available for an experienced Design Manager with a strong interior design background to join a growing property and hospitality group based in Fortitude Valley.

This is not a traditional architecture-led Design Manager position. The business is looking for someone with creative flair, a strong eye for finishes, materials and spaces, and the ability to translate ideas into practical design outcomes across a diverse portfolio of hospitality, retail and accommodation assets.

Working closely with Project Managers and broader business stakeholders, you will help shape and maintain the design identity across the portfolio while also getting hands-on with smaller design projects.

The Role
As Design Manager, you will take ownership of design standards and provide creative design support across multiple business units and asset classes.

Key responsibilities will include:
  • Create, refine and maintain design specifications and document libraries across the portfolio
  • Ensure consistency and compliance with agreed design standards across different asset classes
  • Undertake design reviews and provide recommendations across projects
  • Deliver smaller in-house design projects such as accommodation room and amenities refreshes
  • Support Project Managers with QA and defect reviews
  • Assist with RFIs relating to finishes, materials and design intent
  • Provide design advice across capital expenditure projects
  • Contribute to value management reviews, including alternative finishes and product selections
  • Balance design outcomes with practical cost considerations
  • Produce 3D elevations and visual concepts to support project presentations where required
About You
The key to this position is your interior design capability and creative eye. You may already hold a Design Manager title, or you could be a strong Interior Designer ready to step into a broader position.

Ideally, you will bring:
  • Formal qualifications in Interior Design or a related discipline
  • Strong experience across interior design, preferably within hospitality, hotels, retail or commercial environments
  • A strong eye for finishes, materials, colour, furniture and overall design aesthetic
  • Experience developing or maintaining design standards and specifications
  • Ability to review designs and confidently provide creative input and direction
  • Understanding of project budgets and the cost implications of design decisions
  • Experience working alongside Project Managers, contractors and suppliers
  • Capability with relevant design and 3D visualisation software
  • A practical, collaborative approach with the confidence to take ownership of design decisions
Importantly, the business is not looking for someone who is heavily architecture or technically focused. They are looking for someone who brings genuine artistic flair and interior design sensibility, while still understanding how their ideas translate into real-world projects.

If you are an experienced Interior Designer or Design Manager looking to move into a broader client-side environment where your creativity will be genuinely valued, we would love to hear from you. Reach out to Monique @ Stellar

job.title: Senior Project Engineer (Marine Piling)
job.description:
About the Company
  
Firmly positioned in Western Australia and nationally as a high-quality, mid-tier civil and marine contracting business, this company is flying in the current market. They have strong financial backing and an impressive sustainable business as they are aligned with several blue-chip mining companies and key public sector clients. They now have an IMMEDIATE need to appoint a SENIOR PROJECT ENGINEER in their high-performance WA team.
  
About the Role
  
As SENIOR PROJECT ENGINEER you will work FIFO 2/1 ex-Perth, to support construction delivery of a large marine project for a blue-chip mining client on WA’s coast. This project will involve multidisciplinary elements of Civil, SMP and electrical works plus marine piling and steel erection being undertaken from a jack-up barge. The SENIOR PROJECT ENGINEER will support the delivery of this multi-disciplinary package of marine construction works by providing technical guidance and coordination planning for the construction delivery team. Also you will lead and mentor younger engineers, and ensure adherence to financial, and contractual parameters. This will involve programming & scheduling the works, planning and reviewing heavy lift studies, weekly and monthly reporting, “cost to complete” forecasting and managing budgets. If you possess proven experience in a similar SENIOR PROJECT ENGINEER/Project Engineer role on marine/piling/structural steel erection projects in an industrial construction environment, you can expect an attractive remuneration package of CIRCA $290K+. This business is also "preferred" status on other marine projects, and tendering multiple upcoming major projects so are well placed to support your career long term. 
  
Skills, Qualifications and Other Requirements
  • Tertiary qualifications in Civil/Structural/Mechanical Engineering
  • 7+ years’ post graduate construction experience as Project Engineer/SENIOR PROJECT ENGINEER for civil/marine contractors in Australia
  • Previous experience managing marine piling and structural steel erection from construction and jack-up barges for jetties, wharves, mooring dolphins, marine load-out facilities or other marine structures
  • Strong contractual and commercial acumen
  • Willingness and ability to undertake 2/1 FIFO roster (ex-Perth)
  • Natural leadership skills and ability to manage client interface
  • WA based with existing rights to work in Australia
  • Available within 4 weeks’ notice period
Benefits
  • Classy & Financially Stable Contracting Business
  • Long-term job security on Marine Projects
  • Superb Salary Package CIRCA $290K+
Company Culture
  
The culture within this construction contractor is renowned as being one that supports career development led by a highly professional management team with an outstanding track record of success. You’ll be warmly welcomed into a construction business operating at the top of the civil industry where your contribution will be valued, acknowledged, and generously rewarded.
